title: Global Trends 2025: A Transformed World
notes: Cover date November 2008; public release reported as 20 November 2008 (day not verified in this capture). Fourth edition. Scope: the four fictionalized global scenarios and the dated or quantified projections the NIC states in its own voice in 'The 2025 Global Landscape' table (pp. iv-v) and the Executive Summary (pp. vi-xii). Body chapters and textboxes (for example 'Technology Breakthroughs by 2025') were not mined. Figures the NIC attributes to others (World Bank food demand +50 percent by 2030) and projections conditional on a stated premise (Russia's GDP approaching the UK's and France's if oil and gas prices stay high) are excluded. Regional/sub-scenarios in the body (four US-China scenarios, a US 'October Surprise' diary) are not captured separately. Horizon 2025 has passed. dni.gov returns 403 to scripts; read from the Wayback copy of the original dni.gov/nic/PDF_2025 file.

entries.label: No single nation-state 'international community' by 2025
entries.quote: By 2025 a single “international community” composed of nation-states will no longer exist.
entries.subject: global power distribution
entries.note: 'The 2025 Global Landscape' table, p. iv.

entries.label: US remains most powerful but less dominant
entries.quote: The United States will remain the single most powerful country but will be less dominant.
entries.subject: US global role
entries.note: Relative certainty, table p. iv. Repeated in the Executive Summary ('By 2025 the US will find itself as one of a number of important actors on the world stage, albeit still the most powerful one').

entries.label: 1.2 billion more people by 2025
entries.quote: Continued economic growth—coupled with 1.2 billion more people by 2025—will put pressure on energy, food, and water resources.
entries.subject: world population
entries.note: Relative certainty, table p. iv.

entries.label: Terrorism unlikely to disappear by 2025
entries.quote: Terrorism is unlikely to disappear by 2025, but its appeal could lessen if economic growth continues in the Middle East and youth unemployment is reduced.
entries.subject: terrorism
entries.note: Relative certainty, table p. iv.

entries.label: Post-WWII international system almost unrecognizable by 2025
entries.quote: The international system—as constructed following the Second World War—will be almost unrecognizable by 2025 owing to the rise of emerging powers, a globalizing economy, an historic transfer of relative wealth and economic power from West to East, and the growing influence of nonstate actors.
entries.subject: global power distribution
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. vi.

entries.label: BRICs match the original G-7's share of global GDP by 2040-2050
entries.quote: Growth projections for Brazil, Russia, India, and China (the BRICs) indicate they will collectively match the original G-7’s share of global GDP by 2040-2050.
entries.subject: global economic power shift
entries.metric: BRIC combined share of global GDP vs original G-7 share
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. vi. Window 2040-2050, beyond the report horizon; target_year set to the end of the window. The 'growth projections' are not attributed in the text.

entries.label: China the world's second largest economy by 2025
entries.quote: If current trends persist, by 2025 China will have the world’s second largest economy
entries.subject: China economy
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. vi. The sentence continues 'and will be a leading military power' (split by a footnote in the PDF). Conditional on current trends. Measure not stated.

entries.label: Sub-Saharan Africa remains most vulnerable region
entries.quote: Sub-Saharan Africa will remain the region most vulnerable to economic disruption, population stresses, civil conflict, and political instability.
entries.subject: Sub-Saharan Africa
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. vii.

entries.label: Many Latin American major countries middle income by 2025; Haiti poorer
entries.quote: Although many of Latin America’s major countries will have become middle income powers by 2025, others, particularly those such as Venezuela and Bolivia that have embraced populist policies for a protracted period, will lag behind—and some, such as Haiti, will have become even poorer and less governable.
entries.subject: Latin America
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. vii.

entries.label: Less than 3 percent of population growth in the West
entries.quote: Asia, Africa, and Latin America will account for virtually all population growth over the next 20 years; less than 3 percent of the growth will occur in the West.
entries.subject: world population
entries.metric: share of world population growth occurring in the West
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. vii. 'Next 20 years' from 2008 read as to 2028; the report horizon is 2025.

entries.label: Youth-bulge countries in the 'arc of instability' down by up to 40 percent
entries.quote: The number of countries with youthful age structures in the current “arc of instability” is projected to decline by as much as 40 percent.
entries.subject: youth bulges
entries.metric: number of countries with youthful age structures in the arc of instability
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. viii. Year implied by the report horizon.

entries.label: Non-OPEC liquids production will not keep up with demand
entries.quote: non-OPEC liquid hydrocarbon production—crude oil, natural gas liquids, and unconventionals such as tar sands— will not grow commensurate with demand.
entries.subject: oil market
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. viii. Context: 'demand is projected to outstrip easily available supplies over the next decade or so'.

entries.label: 36 countries with 1.4 billion people cropland- or freshwater-scarce by 2025
entries.quote: Owing to continuing population growth, 36 countries, with about 1.4 billion people, are projected to fall into this category by 2025.
entries.subject: water scarcity
entries.metric: countries that are cropland or freshwater scarce (population)
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. viii. Baseline in the same paragraph: 21 countries, about 600 million people, 'today'.

entries.label: New energy technologies not commercially viable and widespread by 2025
entries.quote: all current technologies are inadequate for replacing the traditional energy architecture on the scale needed, and new energy technologies probably will not be commercially viable and widespread by 2025.
entries.subject: energy transition
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. viii. The next paragraph says an energy transition by 2025 via photovoltaic, wind and batteries 'cannot be ruled out'.

entries.label: Risk of nuclear weapon use greater than today
entries.quote: The risk of nuclear weapon use over the next 20 years, although remaining very low, is likely to be greater than it is today as a result of several converging trends.
entries.subject: nuclear weapons
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. x. 'Next 20 years' from 2008.

entries.label: No dominant political identity by 2025
entries.quote: No one political identity is likely to be dominant in most societies by 2025.
entries.subject: political identity
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. xi.

entries.label: A World Without the West
entries.quote: In A World Without the West, the new powers supplant the West as the leaders on the world stage.
entries.subject: global order
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. xii. Body: the US withdraws from Central Asia, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization rises while NATO declines, Russia and China form a marriage of convenience.

entries.label: October Surprise
entries.quote: October Surprise illustrates the impact of inattention to global climate change; unexpected major impacts narrow the world’s range of options.
entries.subject: climate change
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. xii. Body: a major hurricane linked to climate change hits New York City and damages the NY Stock Exchange.

entries.label: BRICs' Bust-Up
entries.quote: In BRICs’ Bust-Up, disputes over vital resources emerge as a source of conflict between major powers—in this case two emerging heavyweights—India and China.
entries.subject: great power conflict
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. xii. Outside powers intervene before the China-India clash escalates.

entries.label: Politics is Not Always Local
entries.quote: In Politics is Not Always Local, nonstate networks emerge to set the international agenda on the environment, eclipsing governments.
entries.subject: global order
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. xii. Body: a nonstate coalition helps elect the UN Secretary General and secures a new worldwide climate agreement.
